Fixed in 02e7945 fix(watch): share one expiry test so a sub-millisecond budget times out instead of throwing; regression test tests/watch.test.mjs 'a deadline inside the sub-millisecond window ends the watch as a timeout, never as a thrown deadline error' first (a sweep of 19 deadlines across the window, plus the outOfBudget/withinDeadline agreement asserted directly).

CORRECTION to this bead's original diagnosis: the unguarded snapshot at lib/watch.mjs:149 was NOT the cause. snapshot() is deadline-tolerant — every read goes through its get() wrapper and it returns an incomplete snapshot rather than throwing — and watchRun with an already-expired deadline returns a timeout result cleanly. The real site is lib/watch.mjs:137, the guarded stream wait, and the real cause is a disagreement between two expiry tests: withinDeadline used Math.floor(deadline - now) <= 0 while expired() used now >= deadline, so a remaining budget in (0, 1) ms was 'spent' to the first and 'live' to the second; the catch then rethrew and the error escaped as exit 1. Diagnosed from a captured stack under synthetic load, then reproduced deterministically. Fix: outOfBudget(deadline, signal) exported from snapshot.mjs and used by both.
